source.title: UrbanFM: Scaling Urban Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models
source.authors: Wei Chen; Yu-Qian Wu; Junle Chen; Xiao-Fan Zhou; Yuxuan Liang

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present. Some table layouts are flattened in the text, but the scaling tables can be assigned to datasets and conditions.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling evaluations to urban spatio-temporal forecasting: it varies pre-training data volume and model depth and reports downstream errors. It does not test language-model cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and uses scaling laws as motivation, but cited findings are not rows. Its own relevant outcomes are downstream MAE/RMSE/MAPE for data-volume and depth sweeps. It does not measure held-out pre-training cross-entropy, fit small runs to predict much larger runs, or optimize parameter/token allocation under a fixed compute budget. MAE is recorded for the scaling sweeps; the tables also show RMSE and MAPE, whose trends do not disagree with the MAE trend. Spatial/temporal window-size experiments are not included because those vary input resolution rather than model, data, or compute scale.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps pre-training data volume (ratios 1 to 10) and depth (2 to 10 layers) for an urban spatio-temporal Transformer. It reports zero-shot forecasting error on held-out PEMS datasets, which tests scaling in a non-text modality (V5) and on downstream tasks (V6). It does not measure language-model pretraining loss, fit a power law, extrapolate, or vary compute allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say depth from 2 to 8 layers consistently reduces error, and that all metrics show power-law decay with data, with no saturation at the largest proportion. They predict further data will keep improving zero-shot generalisation. Larger parameter scaling is left as future engineering. They report no fit, and their own 10-layer results are worse than 8 layers.
record.recipe_differences: Urban spatio-temporal forecasting model and downstream MAE/RMSE/MAPE sweeps; not language-model held-out cross-entropy, token/compute sweeps, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Data-volume results vary by dataset and short- versus long-term horizon. Depth results are not strictly monotonic at the largest tested depths in the short-horizon MAE table.
record.peer_reviewed: Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (venue stated)
record.problems: Scaling results are reported on four PEMS datasets, and the data-volume sweep has five ratios. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these scaling tables. The results concern downstream forecasting metrics, not pre-training loss; the reported ratios do not establish prediction from small runs to orders-of-magnitude-larger runs. Depth results have small reversals at higher depths.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 60 rows: all four datasets, both horizons, and all five data ratios for MAE (Table D.5), plus short-horizon MAE at all five layer counts for all four datasets (Table D.6). Omitted the long-horizon depth entries in Table D.6 because of the 60-row cap. RMSE and MAPE from Tables D.5–D.6 are not separate rows because their reported trends do not disagree with MAE. Spatial- and temporal-window sweeps in Tables D.7–D.8 are excluded as input-resolution variation, not tests of the versions' model/data/compute scaling claims.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or exponent is reported. The data sweep spans only one order of magnitude (ratio 1 to 10). Compute is not varied, and parameter count is varied only via depth, with no parameter counts stated.
Downstream performance is not related to pretraining loss. There is no prediction of larger-scale performance from smaller runs.
No extrapolation from fitted small runs.
Depth is not varied at fixed parameter count.
No fitting choices or comparison of published laws.

missing.what: MAPE in the data sweep is not monotone, contrary to rows_left_out's claim that RMSE/MAPE do not disagree. PEMS04 long MAPE rises from 21.75 (ratio 1) to 28.24 (ratio 2). Short MAPE rises from ratio 2 to 4 on PEMS03 (18.96 to 19.70) and PEMS08 (15.40 to 15.64).
Long-horizon depth MAE (declared omitted for the row cap) shows the same pattern: best at 8 layers, worse at 10 in all four datasets (e.g. PEMS07 26.39 to 29.25).
Units of the data ratio: the text says the proportion increases 'from 1%', so ratios 1 to 10 are likely 1% to 10% of WorldST. Row conditions should state this.

record.verdict_notes: The PEMS evaluation sets are marked as not overlapping pre-training, so the sweeps measure held-out zero-shot error in a non-text modality. The default model (8 layers, ratio 10) gives the same values in Tables D.5 and D.6. There is no uncertainty, no seeds, and no parameter counts. The 'power-law' claim is the authors' description, not a fitted result. Rows are linked to both V5 and V6 because PEMS forecasting is both held-out modelling error and a downstream benchmark; readers should not count them twice.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or parameter/token/compute scaling is measured.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation or parameter/token growth law is evaluated.
Depth is varied, but architectures are not compared at fixed parameter count and the paper does not assess whether architecture details have only slight effects.
Tests data-volume scaling for urban spatio-temporal forecasting errors; does not test image/video or the other listed modalities and regimes.
Tests downstream forecasting error against pre-training data volume and model depth; does not test downstream performance against pre-training loss or task predictability across other scales.

Does not compare fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, or compute-optimal splits, nor establish that published laws disagree. Input-window sweeps are not tests of the stated parameter/data/compute scaling fit-dependence.

relationships.condition: Data-volume sweep (ratio 1 to 10), four PEMS datasets, short and long horizons, MAE
relationships.reason: Zero-shot MAE falls monotonically with more pre-training data in all 8 dataset-horizon series (e.g. PEMS07 long 46.10 to 26.39; rows D03S1 to D08L10).
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot MAE decreased monotonically across all eight dataset-horizon series, including a decrease from 46.10 to 26.39 for PEMS07 long-horizon prediction.

relationships.condition: Power-law form of the data sweep
relationships.reason: The authors assert power-law decay but fit none. Over one decade the log-log decline is irregular and steepens at ratios 5 to 10 (e.g. D03L: 28.52, 27.00, 24.21, 20.55, 17.03), not a straight line.
relationships.display_finding: The log-log decline steepened at data ratios 5–10 rather than forming a straight line, with D03L errors of 28.52, 27.00, 24.21, 20.55 and 17.03 across the sweep.

relationships.condition: Model depth sweep, short horizon, all four PEMS datasets
relationships.reason: Error falls from 2 to 6 or 8 layers, then rises at 10 layers in every dataset (and at 8 in three). Model scaling saturates or reverses within 2 to 10 layers (rows DEP*S8 and DEP*S10).
relationships.display_finding: Error decreased through six or eight layers, then rose at ten layers on every dataset and at eight layers on three datasets.

relationships.condition: Data-volume sweep, downstream zero-shot forecasting on four unseen PEMS datasets
relationships.reason: Downstream MAE falls at every larger data ratio across both horizons (rows D03S2 to D08L10).
relationships.display_finding: MAE decreases at every larger data ratio across all four unseen datasets and both forecasting horizons.

relationships.condition: Depth sweep, and MAPE metric in the data sweep
relationships.reason: Downstream error rises again at 10 layers (rows DEP*S10). By the text's Table D.5, MAPE is non-monotone: PEMS04 long rises from 21.75 to 28.24 at ratio 2.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream error rose again at 10 layers, and PEMS04 long-horizon MAPE increased from 21.75 to 28.24 at data ratio 2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: UrbanFM data-volume sweep across PEMS03, PEMS04, PEMS07, and PEMS08, short- and long-term forecasting
reader_labels.reason: The paper states that downstream MAE, RMSE, and MAPE decay as pre-training data proportion increases; MAE falls across the reported ratios in rows D03S1–D08L10.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Increasing pre-training data ratios on the four PEMS datasets, short and long horizons
reader_labels.reason: Downstream MAE is lower at every reported ratio above 1 than at the ratio-1 reference in rows D03S2–D08L10; the authors characterize the metric trends as power-law decay.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Short-horizon depth sweep on PEMS03, PEMS04, PEMS07, and PEMS08
reader_labels.reason: Errors are lower than the 2-layer reference at larger depths, but MAE rises again at some 8- or 10-layer settings relative to the best intermediate depth (rows DEP03S8–DEP08S10).
